scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapters 8-10 (Part II: Assets, rules, and institutions), with the exchange-rate claims of Ch24 and the real-bills claim of Ch11. Indexed and foreign debt, currency pegs and the gold standard; capital structure and the cashless limit; maturity as a buffer; default and haircuts; central-bank independence; better rules: inflation targets (0 < alpha < 2), fiscal rules (only P = P* under perfect foresight; false in general under uncertainty with an explicit sunspot tree; restored for prices bounded on one side), the fiscal Taylor rule, mixed debt rules, spread targets and swaps, an indexed-debt peg and a CPI standard; pots of assets, shares as money, balance sheets; separate versus common surplus pools and the exchange rate. Printed errors corrected with Lean counterexamples. Genuine probability models: a measure-theoretic expectation system (Mathlib conditional expectation on a filtered probability space, bounded measurable processes, almost-sure statements, bridges both ways to the core finite-tree systems, a genuine i.i.d. infinite-product economy that is not finitely supported) and the chapter's stochastic results re-proved there.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapters 8-10, pp. 238-311; also pp. 322 and 527.
